title: Statistics, B.S. (Eberly College of Science)
notes: Statistics and Computing Option, University Park (the bulletin's other four options are Actuarial Statistics, Applied Statistics, Biostatistics, and Graduate Study — Statistics and Computing is the general/data-science-focused track, distinct from Actuarial Science's existing ACTSC major). 'etm' marks the gateway courses (Calc I, STAT 200) everything downstream depends on. Post-rescrape correction: the prior note here claimed STAT 184's 'MATH 21' prereq was a placement threshold patched into stat_catalog.json's concurrent_groups -- after the fresh re-scrape (catalogs are no longer hand-patched), both STAT 200 and STAT 184 have a real, literal 'MATH 21' prereq (no OR alternatives, no concurrent path) that MATH 140/141 doesn't satisfy. Added the real MATH 3 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 21 chain (MATH 21 needs MATH 4, which needs MATH 3) across Semesters 1-3, ahead of STAT 200/184 which now land in Semester 4 instead of Semester 1 -- STAT 300/380/400/470W all cascade from STAT 200/184 and shift accordingly. Same fix pattern as LSCPE-2026.json. 2026-08-27 verification against the live bulletin's fully-enumerated Statistics and Computing Option lists found this plan's own notes already claimed '12 credits across 4 slots' for the Advanced STAT elective pool, but the actual JSON only had 3 slots (9 credits) -- a real documentation-vs-implementation gap. Fixed by adding a 4th slot and wiring all 4 to the bulletin's real enumerated list (see each item's own notes) instead of a fully generic placeholder. Also found 'Supporting Courses and Related Areas: Select 8 credits from department list' modeled as a single 3-credit slot -- added 2 more (reaching the real 8 credits) and wired via open_elective. Widened the 'CMPSC 360' item to include the bulletin's real 'or MATH 311W' alternate. Added IE and BBH/HPA to this plan's departments list since the real Advanced elective list draws from them. These additions (8 more credits: 3 for the elective pool, 5 for Supporting Courses) pushed the plan past what fit at the original 17cr/semester cap, so max_credits_per_semester was raised to 18, the same precedent used across dozens of other majors' plans (see PHYS-2026.json's notes for the fuller rationale).
